message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"16","text":"Nevertheless, all of you should know that the bishop toils more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, but he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, preside as a helper to each person as far as you are able, taking upon yourself the cares of everyone. Hence, in undertaking to have you administer, I know that I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and endure nobly, knowing that when you reach the harbor of rest, God will repay you with the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because, for the salvation of all, you undertook the greater toil. So if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise that arises from injustice, but through righteous administration pursue the beneficial praise that comes from Christ.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν προκαθέσθητι βοηθός","chosen":"preside as a helper to each person as far as you are able","rationale":"προκαθέσθητι denotes taking the leading or presiding position, while βοηθός defines that position as one of assistance."},{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι","chosen":"in undertaking to have you administer","rationale":"The rendering takes σέ as the subject of οἰκονομεῖν and Peter as the subject of ἀναδέξασθαι."},{"source_quote":"ἀναφαίρετον μισθόν","chosen":"an inalienable reward","rationale":"ἀναφαίρετον describes something that cannot be taken away."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐπ’ ἄκρον δικαιοσύνην","chosen":"righteousness carried to the utmost","rationale":"The wording preserves the intensifying image of righteousness extending to the limit."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον","chosen":"pursue the beneficial praise that comes from Christ","rationale":"θηρεύειν is literally to hunt or pursue, and ἐπωφελῆ characterizes the praise as beneficial."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὅθεν τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς","issue":"The nesting of the infinitives permits more than one syntactic construal, particularly whether σέ is the subject or object of οἰκονομεῖν. The translation takes Clement as the one who is to administer and Peter as the one who has received the favor.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"17","text":"After saying these things and many more besides, he again looked toward the multitude and said, “And you also, my beloved brothers and fellow servants, yield in every respect to the one presiding over truth, knowing this: the one who grieves him has not received Christ, whose chair has been entrusted to him; and, as one who has not received Christ, he will be reckoned as one who has rejected the Father. Therefore, he will be cast out of the good kingdom. For this reason, strive to attend every assembly, so that you may not, as deserters, incur a charge of sin because of the commander’s discouragement. Therefore, above all else, all of you should be concerned for him, knowing that through each of you the evil one wages war against him alone with greater hostility. So strive to continue in affection toward him and goodwill toward one another, and to obey him, so that he too may be relieved and you may be able to be saved.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷ προκαθεζομένῳ ἀληθείας","chosen":"the one presiding over truth","rationale":"The genitive with προκαθεζομένῳ is taken as identifying that over which the person presides."},{"source_quote":"χριστόν, οὗ τὴν καθέδραν πεπίστευται","chosen":"Christ, whose chair has been entrusted to him","rationale":"The passive πεπίστευται presents the presiding figure as entrusted with Christ’s chair; Christ functions here as a personal designation."},{"source_quote":"ὡς λειποτάκται","chosen":"as deserters","rationale":"λειποτάκτης is a military term for someone who abandons an assigned rank or post."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῆς τοῦ ταξιάρχου ἀθυμίας ἁμαρτίας ἔγκλημα λάβητε","chosen":"incur a charge of sin because of the commander’s discouragement","rationale":"The military image in ταξίαρχος is retained, while ὑπό is read causally with the commander’s loss of heart."},{"source_quote":"αὐτῷ ἐπακούειν","chosen":"obey him","rationale":"In this exhortatory context, ἐπακούειν means responding submissively rather than merely hearing."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"18","text":"You should also understand some things on your own, because he cannot speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not associate with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his purpose, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, laying claim to have everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his instruction. But if anyone remains a friend to those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, he himself is also one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—far worse than the enemies who appear openly, scattering those within under the guise of friendship.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷδε μὴ προσαμιλλᾶσθαι","chosen":"Do not associate with this person","rationale":"Although προσαμιλλᾶσθαι can denote engaging or contending with someone, the surrounding references to friendship and social contact support the broader relational sense here."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν","chosen":"laying claim to have everyone as friends","rationale":"The middle ἐπιδικαζόμενος expresses asserting a claim, here directed toward the stated aim of having everyone as friends."},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας","chosen":"heeding his instruction","rationale":"ὁμιλία can mean discourse or instruction; this sense fits the requirement to heed the presiding figure."},{"source_quote":"τῷ σώματι συνὼν ὑμῖν, τῇ γνώμῃ μὴ ὢν μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν","chosen":"although he is with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose","rationale":"The rendering preserves the source’s contrast between bodily presence and inward intention."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ δοκούσης φιλίας","chosen":"under the guise of friendship","rationale":"δοκούσης marks the friendship as seeming or apparent rather than genuine."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται, τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας","issue":"The antecedents of both occurrences of αὐτός are not explicit. They most naturally refer to the presiding leader, but the clause could instead be understood with reference to the alienated person. The translation preserves the pronouns rather than resolving them by adding a named antecedent.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"19","text":"After saying these things, there in the midst of everyone, he laid his hands on me and urged me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are here with me, I charge you: whenever I depart from this present life—as is owed to me—send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account, including even the reflections you have had since childhood and how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, listening to the words and deeds proclaimed by me from city to city. Then, at the end, do not hesitate also to make known the cause of my death, as I foretold it. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that I have piously discharged what I was in every way bound to suffer. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me the teacher’s chair was entrusted not to an unlearned man ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule. For deceptive discourse destroys the souls of the crowds who listen.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν","chosen":"urged me to sit","rationale":"δυσώπησε here means that Peter prevailed upon or strongly entreated Clement; the infinitive supplies what he urged him to do."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν","chosen":"the reflections you have had since childhood","rationale":"λογισμοί denotes thoughts or reflections, and ἐκ παίδων locates them from childhood onward."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν","chosen":"the cause of my death","rationale":"πρόφασις can mean occasion, cause, or pretext; the account of the death calls for the causal sense here."},{"source_quote":"ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην","chosen":"I have piously discharged what I was in every way bound to suffer","rationale":"ἀπεδόμην is read as the aorist middle of ἀποδίδωμι, presenting the required suffering as an obligation duly rendered or discharged."},{"source_quote":"ἐκκλησίας κανόνα","chosen":"the church’s rule","rationale":"κανών denotes an authoritative norm, standard, or rule rather than necessarily a later fixed collection of texts."},{"source_quote":"πλάνος γὰρ ὁμιλία","chosen":"For deceptive discourse","rationale":"πλάνος characterizes the discourse as misleading or deceptive, while ὁμιλία here denotes teaching or discourse."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν.","issue":"The printed period separates the infinitive καθεσθῆναί from the finite verb ἐδυσώπησεν that most naturally governs it. This appears to be editorial punctuation rather than a missing word.","proposed_reading":"καθεσθῆναί με ἐδυσώπησεν.","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι","issue":"The construction blends ὅπως with an accusative-and-infinitive clause in σὲ ... διαπέμψαι. The intended request is evident, but the supplied syntax is irregular. The translation construes the infinitive as dependent on Ἀξιῶ.","proposed_reading":"ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν","issue":"The printed period interrupts the coordinated description before οὐκ εἰδώς, and the scope of the first οὐκ across the coordinated descriptors is syntactically loose. Context indicates that the entire description—unlearned, ignorant of life-giving words, and not knowing the church’s rule—is negated.","proposed_reading":"οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"20","text":"Therefore I, my lord James, when he had said these things and I had given my promise, did not delay. As I had been commanded, I arranged under headings the greater part of the discourses delivered from city to city, which had already been written to you beforehand and sent by him in books, as a kind of reminder, and sent them to you in this form, giving the work the title “Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings during His Sojourns.” But I will now begin to set it out as I was commanded.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ πολὺ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν λόγων","chosen":"the greater part of the discourses delivered from city to city","rationale":"τὸ πολύ denotes the greater part or bulk, while κατὰ πόλιν distributes the discourses by city."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ κεφαλαίων ποιῆσαι","chosen":"arranged under headings","rationale":"κεφάλαια are summary headings or principal points used to organize an epitome."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ σημείου χάριν","chosen":"as a kind of reminder","rationale":"σημεῖον is a sign or marker; in the context of summary headings it functions as an aid to recall."},{"source_quote":"Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή","chosen":"Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings during His Sojourns","rationale":"ἐπιδήμια describes the preachings in relation to Peter’s stays or sojourns in the various places visited."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐκτιθέναι ὡς ἐκελεύσθην ἄρξομαι","chosen":"I will now begin to set it out as I was commanded","rationale":"ἄρξομαι governs the articular infinitive and marks the transition from the letter to the promised exposition."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
